reconstructed_theorem_text: For every real m (no sign or nonzero assumption), there exists a measure γ on ℝ×ℝ whose first marginal is (1/2)N(−m,1)+(1/2)N(m,1) and second marginal is (1/4)N(−m,1)+(3/4)N(m,1), where N(a,1) is the real Gaussian probability law of mean a and variance one. The same γ has nonnegative quadratic transport integral ∫ℝ² |x−y|² dγ(x,y)=m², with the equality interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals by embedding m²; the cost is finite for every real m. The specified marginals imply γ is a probability measure.
objects: A real m, the actual two Gaussian-mixture marginals, and a measure γ on ℝ×ℝ.
domains: The product real line and the nonnegative quadratic integral in the extended nonnegative reals.
quantifiers: For every real m; the same γ has both prescribed marginals and the exact cost, and may depend on m.
assumptions: No sign or nonzero assumption on m.
conclusion: The same γ has nonnegative quadratic transport integral ∫ℝ² |x−y|² dγ(x,y)=m², with the equality interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals by embedding m²; the cost is finite for every real m.
scopes: γ may depend on m; this is an existence assertion for a joint measure with exact cost, not an optimality/uniqueness claim or equality for the Wasserstein infimum/distance, and it specifies neither a transport map nor a coupling construction.
constant_dependencies: Constants are fixed mixture weights and common variance one.
